question: Consider the lines $\vec{r}=(\hat{i}+2\hat{j})+\lambda(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})$ and $\vec{r}=(\hat{j}+\hat{k})+\mu(2\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+4\hat{k})$. Without finding their point of intersection, decide whether the lines are coplanar.
explanation: Step 1: The direction vectors of the two lines are $\vec{b_1}=(1,-1,2)$ and $\vec{b_2}=(2,-2,4)$. Step 2: These vectors satisfy $\vec{b_2}=2\vec{b_1}$. Therefore, the two lines have parallel directions. Step 3: The given points on the lines are $(1,2,0)$ and $(0,1,1)$ respectively. Their difference $(-1,-1,1)$ is not proportional to $(1,-1,2)$, so the two equations represent distinct parallel lines rather than the same line. Step 4: Any two distinct parallel lines in three-dimensional space lie in a common plane. Step 5: Therefore, no intersection calculation is required. The two given lines are parallel and hence are coplanar.

options.A: They are skew because they are parallel.
options.B: They are coplanar because their direction vectors are proportional, so the lines are parallel.
options.C: They are non-coplanar because the given points are distinct.
options.D: They are coplanar only if they intersect.
